sentences.zh: 25%唐都長安，而關中號稱沃野，然其土地狹，所出不足以給京師，備水旱，故常轉漕東南之粟。

translations.literal: The Tang capital was Chang'an, and Guanzhong was famed as fertile land, yet its territory was narrow and its yield insufficient to supply the capital, guard against flood and drought, and so grain from the southeast was regularly transported by canal.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang made Chang'an their capital, and although Guanzhong was renowned as rich farmland, the region was cramped and could not produce enough to feed the court or buffer against flood and drought; grain from the southeast therefore had to be shipped in by canal on a regular basis.

sentences.zh: 高祖、太宗之時，用物有節而易贍，水陸漕運，歲不過二十萬石，故漕事簡。

translations.literal: In the times of Gaozu and Taizong, expenditures were restrained and supplies easy to meet; grain transport by water and land did not exceed two hundred thousand shi per year, and so canal transport affairs were simple.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu and Taizong, the court spent with restraint and provisions were readily met; combined water and land transport moved no more than two hundred thousand shi of grain a year, and canal logistics remained straightforward.

sentences.zh: 自高宗已後，歲益增多，而功利繁興，民亦罹其弊矣。

translations.literal: From Gaozong onward the annual amount steadily increased; profit-seeking projects flourished, and the people also suffered their harms.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong, the annual volume grew year by year, ambitious public works multiplied, and the people bore the cost.

sentences.zh: 初，江淮漕租米至東都輸含嘉倉，以車或馱陸運至陝。

translations.literal: At first, canal-rent grain from Jianghuai reached the Eastern Capital and was delivered to the Hanjia Granary, then carried overland by cart or pack animal to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Jianghuai tribute grain was shipped to Luoyang and stored in the Hanjia Granary, then hauled overland by cart or pack train to Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 而水行來遠，多風波覆溺之患，其失嘗十七八，故其率一斛得八斗為成勞。

translations.literal: But the water route was long, with many losses to wind and waves and capsizing; losses often reached seven or eight tenths, so the standard was that eight dou from one hu counted as completed labor.
translations.idiomatic: The river leg was long and perilous; wind and waves often claimed seven or eight tenths of the cargo, so only eight dou delivered from each hu was counted as a full haul.

sentences.zh: 而陸運至陝，纔三百里，率兩斛計傭錢千。

translations.literal: Yet overland transport to Shan was only three hundred li, and for every two hu the hire was reckoned at a thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Overland hauls to Shan covered barely three hundred li, yet hire for every two hu ran to a thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 民送租者，皆有水陸之直，而河有三門底柱之險。

translations.literal: People delivering rent all paid water and land transport fees, and the river had the perils of Sanmen and Dizhu.
translations.idiomatic: Rent-bearers paid both river and road charges, and the Yellow River gorge at Sanmen and the Dizhu reefs made the route deadly.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，苑西監褚朗議鑿三門山為梁，可通陸運。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, Garden-West Supervisor Chu Lang proposed cutting Sanmen Mountain for a beam bridge to open overland transport.
translations.idiomatic: In 656, Chu Lang, supervisor of the western park, proposed cutting through Sanmen Mountain for a beam bridge so grain could move by land.

sentences.zh: 乃發卒六千鑿之，功不成。

translations.literal: Six thousand laborers were mobilized to cut it, but the work did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand conscripts were sent to cut the pass, but the project failed.

sentences.zh: 其後，將作大匠楊務廉又鑿為棧，以輓漕舟。

translations.literal: Later, Chief Artisan of the Directorate Yang Wulian again cut plank roads to haul canal boats.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Yang Wulian, chief artisan of the Directorate of Works, cut plank roads along the cliffs to haul grain barges.

sentences.zh: 輓夫繫二鈲於胸，而繩多絕，輓夫輒墜死，則以逃亡報，因繫其父母妻子，人以為苦。

translations.literal: Haulers fastened two hooks to their chests; ropes often broke and haulers would fall to their deaths, which was reported as flight, and then their parents, wives, and children were bound—people regarded it as bitter suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Trackers wore two chest hooks on ropes that snapped constantly; when a man fell to his death, officials reported him as a deserter and imprisoned his family—an ordeal the people found unbearable.

sentences.zh: 開元十八年，宣州刺史裴耀卿朝集京師，玄宗訪以漕事，耀卿條上便宜曰：「江南戶口多，而無征防之役。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kaiyuan, Xuanzhou Prefect Pei Yaoqing came to the capital for the court assembly; Xuanzong inquired about canal transport, and Yaoqing itemized advantages, saying: "Jiangnan has a large population yet no frontier garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: In 730, Pei Yaoqing of Xuanzhou came to Chang'an for the annual assembly; when Xuanzong asked about canal transport, he laid out a plan: "Jiangnan is populous yet free of frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 然送租、庸、調物，以歲二月至揚州入斗門，四月已後，始渡淮入汴，常苦水淺，六七月乃至河口，而河水方漲，須八九月水落始得上河入洛，而漕路多梗，船檣阻隘。

translations.literal: Yet in delivering rent, yong, and diao goods, in the second month of the year they reach Yangzhou and enter the Dou Gate; only after the fourth month do they cross the Huai into the Bian, often suffering shallow water; only in the sixth or seventh month do they reach the river mouth, when the river water is rising; only when the water falls in the eighth or ninth month can they ascend the river into Luoyang—and the canal route has many blockages and masts crowd narrow passages.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rent, corvée cloth, and diao goods leave in the second month for Yangzhou and the Dou Gate, cross the Huai into the Bian only after the fourth, struggle through shallows, reach the river mouth in summer when the flood is rising, and cannot enter the Yellow River and Luoyang until the eighth or ninth month when the water falls—so the route is choked and convoys jam the channel.

sentences.zh: 江南之人，不習河事，轉雇河師水手，重為勞費。

translations.literal: People of Jiangnan are unskilled in river affairs and repeatedly hire river pilots and sailors, doubling labor and expense.
translations.idiomatic: Southerners know little of river work and must hire pilots and crews at heavy cost.

sentences.zh: 其得行日少，阻滯日多。

translations.literal: Days when they can sail are few; days of delay are many.
translations.idiomatic: Sailing days are few and waiting days many.

sentences.zh: 今漢、隋漕路，瀕河倉廩，遺迹可尋。

translations.literal: Now the Han and Sui canal routes, with granaries along the river, have traces that can still be traced.
translations.idiomatic: The Han and Sui canal system, with riverside granaries, still leaves traces we can follow.

sentences.zh: 可於河口置武牢倉，鞏縣置洛口倉，使江南之舟不入黃河，黃河之舟不入洛口。

translations.literal: At the river mouth one may place the Wulao Granary, and at Gong County the Luokou Granary, so that Jiangnan boats do not enter the Yellow River and Yellow River boats do not enter Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: Build the Wulao Granary at the river mouth and the Luokou Granary at Gong County, so Jiangnan craft never enter the Yellow River and Yellow River craft never enter Luokou.

sentences.zh: 而河陽、柏崖、太原、永豐、渭南諸倉，節級轉運，水通則舟行，水淺則寓於倉以待，則舟無停留，而物不耗失。

translations.literal: With the granaries at Heyang, Boya, Taiyuan, Yongfeng, and Weinan, relay transport by stages—when water is open boats sail, when shallow they lodge in granaries to wait—then boats have no long stops and goods suffer no loss.
translations.idiomatic: Relay through Heyang, Boya, Taiyuan, Yongfeng, and Weinan: sail when the channel is deep, store in granaries when it is low, and boats need not linger while grain is spared spoilage.

sentences.zh: 此甚利也。

translations.literal: This would be greatly advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: The savings would be enormous."

sentences.zh: 」玄宗初不省。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong at first did not grasp it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong at first did not take his meaning.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，耀卿為京兆尹，京師雨水，穀踊貴，玄宗將幸東都，復問耀卿漕事，耀卿因請「罷陝陸運，而置倉河口，使江南漕舟至河口者，輸粟於倉而去，縣官雇舟以分入河、洛。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Yaoqing was Jingzhao Intendant; the capital had rain and floods and grain prices soared; Xuanzong was about to visit the Eastern Capital and again asked Yaoqing about canal transport. Yaoqing therefore requested: "Abolish the Shan overland route and place granaries at the river mouth, so that Jiangnan canal boats reaching the mouth unload grain at the granary and depart, and the government hire boats to distribute into the river and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: In 733, as Jingzhao intendant, he faced flood-driven grain panic as the emperor prepared to move to Luoyang; asked again, he urged ending the Shan overland haul, building granaries at the river mouth where southern boats would unload and leave, and having the state hire craft to relay cargo up the Yellow River and into the Luo.

sentences.zh: 置倉三門東西，漕舟輸其東倉，而陸運以輸西倉，復以舟漕，以避三門之水險。

translations.literal: Place granaries east and west of Sanmen; canal boats deliver to the east granary, overland transport carries to the west granary, then boats again by canal, to avoid Sanmen's water perils.
translations.idiomatic: Build granaries east and west of Sanmen: barges unload at the east store, porters relay to the west store, then boats resume the river leg and skirt Sanmen's rapids."

sentences.zh: 」玄宗以為然。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃於河陰置河陰倉，河清置柏崖倉；

translations.literal: Then at Heyin the Heyin Granary was placed, and at Heqing the Boya Granary;
translations.idiomatic: They built the Heyin Granary at Heyin and the Boya Granary at Heqing;

sentences.zh: 三門東置集津倉，西置鹽倉；

translations.literal: east of Sanmen the Jijin Granary, west the Yan Granary;
translations.idiomatic: the Jijin Granary east of Sanmen and the Yan Granary to the west;

sentences.zh: 鑿山十八里以陸運。

translations.literal: and the mountain was cut for eighteen li of overland transport.
translations.idiomatic: and cut an eighteen-li mountain road for the overland relay.

sentences.zh: 自江、淮漕者，皆輸河陰倉，自河陰西至太原倉，謂之北運，自太原倉浮渭以實關中。

translations.literal: All grain transported from the Jiang and Huai was delivered to the Heyin Granary; from Heyin west to the Taiyuan Granary was called the Northern Transport; from Taiyuan Granary they floated on the Wei to fill Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Huai grain all went to Heyin; the leg west to Taiyuan was called the Northern Transport, and from Taiyuan barges went down the Wei to supply Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 玄宗大悅，拜耀卿為黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事，兼江淮都轉運使，以鄭州刺史崔希逸、河南少尹蕭炅為副使，益漕晉、絳、魏、濮、邢、貝、濟、博之租輸諸倉，轉而入渭。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was greatly pleased, appointed Yaoqing Yellow Gate Attendant-Councilor and Associate Chief Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrently Chief Transport Commissioner for Jianghuai, with Zhengzhou Prefect Cui Xiyi and Henan Vice Intendant Xiao Jiong as deputies, increasing transport of rent from Jin, Jiang, Wei, Pu, Xing, Bei, Ji, and Bo into the granaries and relaying into the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Xuanzong made him vice president of the Secretariat, chief councillor, and Jianghuai transport commissioner, with Cui Xiyi and Xiao Jiong as deputies, and added rent grain from eight north China prefectures into the relay system feeding the Wei.

sentences.zh: 凡三歲，漕七百萬石，省陸運傭錢三十萬緡。

translations.literal: In all three years, seven million shi were transported by canal, saving three hundred thousand strings in overland hire.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years they moved seven million shi and saved three hundred thousand strings in overland wages.

sentences.zh: 是時，民久不罹兵革，物力豐富，朝廷用度亦廣，不計道里之費，而民之輸送所出水陸之直，增以「函脚」、「營窖」之名，民間傳言用斗錢運斗米，其糜耗如此。

translations.literal: At this time the people had long been free of war, goods were abundant, and court expenditures were also broad; distance costs were not counted, yet on top of water and land transport fees paid in delivery were added charges named "crate-foot" and "camp-pit," and popular rumor said it took a dou of cash to move a dou of rice—such was the waste.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had left the realm prosperous and the court lavish; on top of legitimate transport fees, collectors added surcharges called "crate-foot" and "camp-pit," until people said it cost a peck of cash to ship a peck of grain.

sentences.zh: 及耀卿罷相，北運頗艱，米歲至京師纔百萬石。

translations.literal: When Yaoqing left the chancellorship, the Northern Transport grew quite difficult, and grain reaching the capital each year was only one million shi.
translations.idiomatic: After Yaoqing left office the northern route faltered, and only a million shi a year reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，遂罷北運。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Northern Transport was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 737 the northern route was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 而崔希逸為河南陝運使，歲運百八十萬石。

translations.literal: Cui Xiyi served as Henan-Shan transport commissioner and moved 1.8 million shi per year.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiyi, as Henan-Shan transport commissioner, still moved 1.8 million shi annually.

sentences.zh: 其後以太倉積粟有餘，歲減漕數十萬石。

translations.literal: Later, because the Ever-Normal Granary had surplus grain, several hundred thousand shi were cut from annual canal transport.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with the Ever-Normal Granary overflowing, annual quotas were trimmed by several hundred thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，陝郡太守李齊物鑿砥柱為門以通漕，開其山顛為輓路，燒石沃醯而鑿之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Shan Prefect Li Qiwu cut the Dizhu reefs into a gate for canal passage, opened the mountain crest for a haul road, and cut rock by heating stone and pouring vinegar.
translations.idiomatic: In 741, Shan prefect Li Qiwu cut a gate through the Dizhu reefs, opened a haul road along the cliff top, and used fire and vinegar to fracture the rock.

sentences.zh: 然棄石入河，激水益湍怒，舟不能入新門，候其水漲，以人輓舟而上。

translations.literal: Yet discarded stone entered the river, stirring the water to greater turbulence; boats could not enter the new gate and waited for the flood to rise, then men hauled boats upstream.
translations.idiomatic: Rubble dumped into the river made the current fiercer; boats could not use the new gate until the flood rose, when teams hauled them through.

sentences.zh: 天子疑之，遣宦者按視，齊物厚賂使者，還言便。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven doubted it and sent eunuchs to inspect; Qiwu bribed the envoys heavily, and they returned saying it was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent eunuchs to inspect; Qiwu bribed them lavishly, and they reported the project sound.

sentences.zh: 齊物入為鴻臚卿，以長安令韋堅代之，兼水陸運使。

translations.literal: Qiwu entered office as Minister of Ceremonies; Chang'an Magistrate Wei Jian replaced him and also held the water-land transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiwu became Minister of Ceremonies; Wei Jian, magistrate of Chang'an, replaced him as combined water-land transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 堅治漢、隋運渠，起關門，抵長安，通山東租賦。

translations.literal: Jian repaired the Han and Sui transport canals from Tong Pass to Chang'an, opening Shandong rent and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jian restored the Han and Sui canals from Tong Pass to Chang'an to bring Shandong tribute to the capital.

sentences.zh: 乃絕灞、滻，並渭而東，至永豐倉與渭合。

translations.literal: He cut off the Ba and Chan, joined the Wei eastward, and reached the Yongfeng Granary where it met the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He diverted the Ba and Chan rivers into the Wei eastward to the Yongfeng Granary.

sentences.zh: 又於長樂坡瀕苑牆鑿潭於望春樓下，以聚漕舟。

translations.literal: He also cut a pool below Wangchun Tower on Changle Slope along the park wall to gather canal boats.
translations.idiomatic: Below Wangchun Tower on Changle Slope he excavated a basin along the imperial park wall to berth the grain fleet.

sentences.zh: 堅因使諸舟各揭其郡名，陳其土地所產寶貨諸奇物於栿上。

translations.literal: Jian had each boat display its commandery name and array on the beams the precious goods and curiosities its land produced.
translations.idiomatic: Each barge bore its prefecture's name and displayed local treasures on its deck beams.

sentences.zh: 先時民間唱俚歌曰「得体紇那邪」。

translations.literal: Earlier the people sang a folk song saying "Deti he na ye."
translations.idiomatic: A folk song had long run, "Deti he na ye."

sentences.zh: 其後得寶符於桃林，於是陝縣尉崔成甫更得体歌為得寶弘農野。

translations.literal: Later a treasure talisman was obtained at Taolin, and Shan County Assistant Magistrate Cui Chengfu changed the "deti" song to "Treasure found in the wilds of Hongnong."
translations.idiomatic: When a treasure talisman was found at Taolin, assistant magistrate Cui Chengfu rewrote the refrain as "Treasure found in the Hongnong wilds."

sentences.zh: 堅命舟人為吳、楚服，大笠、廣袖、芒屩以歌之。

translations.literal: Jian ordered boatmen dressed in Wu and Chu garb—large hats, wide sleeves, straw sandals—to sing it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jian dressed the boatmen in Wu and Chu costume—broad hats, wide sleeves, straw sandals—to perform the song.

sentences.zh: 成甫又廣之為歌辭十闋，自衣缺後綠衣、錦半臂、紅抹額，立第一船為號頭以唱，集兩縣婦女百餘人，鮮服靚粧，鳴鼓吹笛以和之。

translations.literal: Chengfu expanded it into ten stanzas; he himself wore green after the que, brocade half-sleeves, and a red forehead band, stood on the lead boat as caller to sing, and gathered over a hundred women from two counties in bright dress and fine makeup, with drums, pipes, and flutes to harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Chengfu expanded it to ten stanzas, stood on the lead boat in green robes, brocade half-sleeves, and a red forehead cloth to lead the chorus, and mustered more than a hundred brightly dressed women from two counties with drums, pipes, and flutes.

sentences.zh: 眾艘以次輳樓下，天子望見大悅，賜其潭名曰廣運潭。

translations.literal: The fleet in turn gathered below the tower; the Son of Heaven saw it from afar and was greatly pleased, naming the pool Broad Transport Pool.
translations.idiomatic: The flotilla filed past the tower; the delighted emperor named the basin Broad Transport Pool.

sentences.zh: 是歲，漕山東粟四百萬石。

translations.literal: That year, four million shi of Shandong grain were transported by canal.
translations.idiomatic: That year four million shi of eastern grain reached the capital by canal.

sentences.zh: 自裴耀卿言漕事，進用者常兼轉運之職，而韋堅為最。

translations.literal: From Pei Yaoqing's counsel on canal affairs, those advanced often also held transport posts, and Wei Jian was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: After Pei Yaoqing's reforms, favored officials often doubled as transport commissioners, and none outdid Wei Jian.

sentences.zh: 初，耀卿興漕路，請罷陸運，而不果廢。

translations.literal: At first Yaoqing opened the canal route and requested abolishing overland transport, but it was not in fact ended.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoqing had sought to end overland hauls when he opened the new route, but the road was never fully abandoned.

sentences.zh: 自景雲中，陸運北路分八遞，雇民車牛以載。

translations.literal: From the Jingyun era the northern overland route was divided into eight relay stages, hiring civilian carts and oxen to carry.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jingyun era the northern road used eight relay stages with hired civilian carts and oxen.

sentences.zh: 開元初，河南尹李傑為水陸運使，運米歲二百五十萬石，而八遞用車千八百乘。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, Henan Intendant Li Jie was water-land transport commissioner, moving 2.5 million shi of rice yearly, while the eight relays used 1,800 carts.
translations.idiomatic: Early Kaiyuan, Henan intendant Li Jie moved 2.5 million shi a year while the eight relays required 1,800 carts.

sentences.zh: 耀卿罷久之，河南尹裴迥以八遞傷牛，乃為交場兩遞，濱水處為宿場，分官總之，自龍門東山抵天津橋為石堰以遏水。

translations.literal: Long after Yaoqing left office, Henan Intendant Pei Jiong, because the eight relays harmed oxen, made two relays at exchange yards, lodging yards along the water, officials assigned to oversee them, and from Longmen's eastern hill to Tianjin Bridge built stone weirs to hold back water.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, Pei Jiong reduced the eight relays to two exchange yards and riverside depots, posted officials along the route, and built stone weirs from Longmen to Tianjin Bridge to tame the current.

sentences.zh: 其後大盜起，而天下匱矣。

translations.literal: Later great rebellion arose and the realm was depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Then the great rebellions broke out and the empire was drained.

sentences.zh: 肅宗末年，史朝義兵分出宋州，淮運於是阻絕，租庸鹽鐵泝漢江而上。

translations.literal: Late in Suzong's reign, Shi Chaoyi's troops issued from Songzhou and Huai transport was cut off; rent, yong, salt, and iron went up the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Suzong's reign, Shi Chaoyi's armies cut the Huai route, and rent, corvée goods, salt, and iron had to go up the Han.

sentences.zh: 河南尹劉晏為戶部侍郎，兼句當度支、轉運、鹽鐵、鑄錢使，江淮粟帛，繇襄、漢越商於以輸京師。

translations.literal: Henan Intendant Liu Yan was Vice Minister of Revenue, concurrently managing fiscal affairs, transport, salt and iron, and coinage; Jianghuai grain and cloth went by Xiang, Han, and over Shangyu to supply the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan of Henan, as vice minister of revenue and fiscal, transport, salt-iron, and coinage commissioner, routed Jianghuai grain and cloth through Xiangyang, the Han, and the Shangyu road to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及代宗出陝州，關中空窘，於是盛轉輸以給用。

translations.literal: When Daizong left Shanzhou, Guanzhong was empty and straitened, and so transport was greatly expanded to supply needs.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong marched out of Shanzhou, starving Guanzhong forced a vast expansion of transport to keep the court fed.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年，廢句當度支使，以劉晏顓領東都、河南、淮西、江南東西轉運、租庸、鑄錢、鹽鐵，轉輸至上都，度支所領諸道租庸觀察使，凡漕事亦皆決於晏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangde the fiscal affairs commissioner was abolished; Liu Yan singly headed transport, rent-yong, coinage, and salt-iron for the Eastern Capital, Henan, Huaixi, and east and west Jiangnan, transport to the supreme capital, and all canal affairs under the fiscal circuit commissioners were also decided by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In 764 the fiscal commissioner post was abolished and Liu Yan took sole charge of transport, rent-yong, coinage, and salt-iron from Luoyang through Henan, Huaixi, and both Jiangnans to the capital; every canal decision passed through him.

sentences.zh: 晏即鹽利顧傭分吏督之，隨江、汴、河、渭所宜。

translations.literal: Yan then used salt profits to hire men and assign officials to supervise, adapting to what suited the Yangtze, Bian, Yellow River, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He used salt revenue to hire crews and post supervisors suited to each leg on the Yangtze, Bian, Yellow River, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 故時轉運船繇潤州陸運至揚子，斗米費錢十九，晏命囊米而載以舟，減錢十五；

translations.literal: Formerly transport boats went by land from Runzhou to Yangzi at nineteen cash per dou of rice; Yan ordered rice bagged and carried by boat, reducing cost by fifteen cash;
translations.idiomatic: The old Runzhou-to-Yangzi leg cost nineteen cash per dou by land; Yan switched to barges and cut fifteen cash;

sentences.zh: 繇揚州距河陰，斗米費錢百二十，晏為歇艎支江船二千艘，每船受千斛，十船為綱，每綱三百人，篙工五十，自揚州遣將部送至河陰，上三門，號「上門填闕船」，米斗減錢九十。

translations.literal: from Yangzhou to Heyin a dou cost 120 cash; Yan built rest-barges and supplied 2,000 river boats, each holding 1,000 hu, ten boats per convoy, 300 men per convoy and fifty polemen; generals escorted from Yangzhou to Heyin and up Sanmen—called "upstream gap-filling boats"—cutting ninety cash per dou.
translations.idiomatic: the Yangzhou-Heyin leg had cost 120 cash per dou; he fielded two thousand river barges of a thousand hu each in convoys of ten with three hundred men and fifty polemen, escorted to Heyin and through Sanmen as "gap-fillers," saving ninety cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 調巴、蜀、襄、漢麻枲竹篠為綯挽舟，以朽索腐材代薪，物無棄者。

translations.literal: He requisitioned hemp, bamboo, and splints from Ba, Shu, Xiang, and Han for towing ropes; used rotten cord and decayed timber for fuel—nothing was wasted.
translations.idiomatic: He sourced hemp, bamboo, and splints from the southwest and Han basin for tow ropes, burned scrap cord and rotten timber for fuel, and wasted nothing.

sentences.zh: 未十年，人人習河險。

translations.literal: Within ten years everyone grew skilled in river hazards.
translations.idiomatic: Within a decade crews mastered the river's dangers.

sentences.zh: 江船不入汴，汴船不入河，河船不入渭；

translations.literal: Yangtze boats did not enter the Bian, Bian boats did not enter the Yellow River, Yellow River boats did not enter the Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Yangtze craft never entered the Bian, Bian craft never the Yellow River, Yellow River craft never the Wei;

sentences.zh: 江南之運積揚州，汴河之運積河陰，河船之運積渭口，渭船之運入太倉。

translations.literal: Jiangnan transport accumulated at Yangzhou, Bian transport at Heyin, river transport at the Wei mouth, and Wei boats delivered into the Ever-Normal Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan grain piled up at Yangzhou, Bian grain at Heyin, Yellow River grain at the Wei mouth, and Wei barges fed the Ever-Normal Granary.

sentences.zh: 歲轉粟百一十萬石，無升斗溺者。

translations.literal: Each year 1.1 million shi of grain were relayed, without a sheng or dou lost to drowning.
translations.idiomatic: He moved 1.1 million shi a year without losing a single peck to the water.

sentences.zh: 輕貨自揚子至汴州，每馱費錢二千二百，減九百，歲省十餘萬緡。

translations.literal: Light goods from Yangzi to Bianzhou cost 2,200 cash per pack load; he cut 900, saving over 100,000 strings yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Light freight from Yangzi to Bianzhou had cost 2,200 cash per load; he cut 900 and saved more than 100,000 strings a year.

sentences.zh: 又分官吏主丹楊湖，禁引溉，自是河漕不涸。

translations.literal: He also assigned officials to manage Danyang Lake, forbidding diversion for irrigation, and from then the river transport did not run dry.
translations.idiomatic: Officials guarded Danyang Lake against irrigation diversions, and the canal stayed navigable.

sentences.zh: 大曆八年，以關內豐穰，減漕十萬石，度支和糴以優農。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dali, because Guanzhong was abundant, canal transport was cut by 100,000 shi and the fiscal office bought grain at fair rates to benefit farmers.
translations.idiomatic: In 773, with Guanzhong abundant, he cut transport by 100,000 shi and the fiscal office bought grain at fair prices to help farmers.

sentences.zh: 晏自天寶末掌出納，監歲運，知左右藏，主財穀三十餘年矣。

translations.literal: Yan from late Tianbao managed receipts and disbursements, oversaw annual transport, and knew the left and right treasuries, directing finances and grain for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: From late Tianbao onward Liu Yan had run receipts, annual transport, and both treasuries for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 及楊炎為相，以舊惡罷晏，轉運使復歸度支，凡江淮漕米，以庫部郎中崔河圖主之。

translations.literal: When Yang Yan became chancellor, he removed Yan over old enmity; transport commissioners returned to the fiscal office, and all Jianghuai canal rice was placed under Repository Section Director Cui Hetu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan became chancellor, old grudges ended Liu Yan's career; transport reverted to the fiscal office and Jianghuai grain passed to Cui Hetu of the repository section.

sentences.zh: 及田悅、李惟岳、李納、梁崇義拒命，舉天下兵討之，諸軍仰給京師。

translations.literal: When Tian Yue, Li Weiyue, Li Na, and Liang Chongyi defied orders, the realm raised armies to attack them, and all forces depended on the capital for supply.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Yue, Li Weiyue, Li Na, and Liang Chongyi rebelled, imperial armies looked to the capital for every ration.

sentences.zh: 而李納、田悅兵守渦口，梁崇義搤襄、鄧，南北漕引皆絕，京師大恐。

translations.literal: Li Na and Tian Yue's troops held Wokou, Liang Chongyi blocked Xiang and Deng, north-south canal routes were all cut, and the capital was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na and Tian Yue held Wokou, Liang Chongyi choked Xiangyang and Nanyang, and with both canal arteries severed the capital panicked.

sentences.zh: 江淮水陸轉運使杜佑以秦、漢運路出浚儀十里入琵琶溝，絕蔡河，至陳州而合，自隋鑿汴河，官漕不通，若導流培岸，功用甚寡；

translations.literal: Jianghuai water-land transport commissioner Du You noted that the Qin-Han route left Junyi ten li into the Pipa Ditch, cut the Cai River, and joined at Chenzhou; since the Sui cut the Bian River official canal transport had not passed—if one diverted flow and raised banks, the labor would be slight;
translations.idiomatic: Du You, Jianghuai transport commissioner, proposed reviving the Qin-Han route from Junyi through Pipa Ditch to Chenzhou; since Sui times the Bian had blocked official transport, but dredging and banking would be light work;

sentences.zh: 疏雞鳴岡首尾，可以通舟，陸行纔四十里，則江、湖、黔中、嶺南、蜀、漢之粟可方舟而下，繇白沙趣東關，歷潁、蔡，涉汴抵東都，無濁河泝淮之阻，減故道二千餘里。

translations.literal: dredging the head and tail of Jiming Hill could open to boats with only forty li overland, so grain from the rivers, lakes, Qianzhong, Lingnan, Shu, and Han could come down in convoys by Baisha to Dongguan, through Ying and Cai, cross the Bian to the Eastern Capital, without the block of the muddy river against the Huai, shortening the old route by more than two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: clearing Jiming Hill would need only forty li of portage, letting grain from the Yangtze basin, southwest, and Han reach Luoyang via Baisha, Ying, Cai, and the Bian without fighting the Huai current—more than two thousand li saved.

sentences.zh: 會李納將李洧以徐州歸命，淮路通而止。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Na's general Li Wei surrendered Xuzhou to the throne, the Huai route opened, and the plan stopped.
translations.idiomatic: But Li Wei's surrender of Xuzhou reopened the Huai route and the project was dropped.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎趙贊又以錢貨出淮迂緩，分置汴州東西水陸運兩稅鹽鐵使，以度支總大綱。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Zhao Zan also held that coin and goods leaving the Huai were slow; he split east and west Bianzhou water-land transport and two-tax salt-iron commissioners, with the fiscal office holding overall control.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zan, vice minister of revenue, split eastern and western Bianzhou transport and two-tax salt-iron commissions because Huai coin shipments were too slow, leaving overall control with the fiscal office.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，關輔宿兵，米斗千錢，太倉供天子六宮之膳不及十日，禁中不能釀酒，以飛龍駝負永豐倉米給禁軍，陸運牛死殆盡。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenyuan, garrison troops in Guanfu made rice a thousand cash per dou; the Ever-Normal Granary could supply the Son of Heaven and six palaces for less than ten days; the inner palace could not brew wine; Flying Dragon camels carried Yongfeng Granary rice to the guard army, and overland transport oxen nearly all died.
translations.idiomatic: Early Zhenyuan, with armies camped in Guanzhong, rice hit a thousand cash per dou; the Ever-Normal Granary could feed court and harem less than ten days; the palace stopped brewing wine; Flying Dragon camels hauled Yongfeng grain to the guards while overland oxen died almost to a beast.

sentences.zh: 德宗以給事中崔造敢言，為能立事，用為相。

translations.literal: Dezong, because Supervising Secretary Cui Zao spoke boldly and could accomplish affairs, used him as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong made outspoken supervising secretary Cui Zao chancellor for his reputation as a doer.

sentences.zh: 造以江、吳素嫉錢穀諸使顓利罔上，乃奏諸道觀察使、刺史選官部送兩稅至京師，廢諸道水陸轉運使及度支巡院、江淮轉運使，以度支、鹽鐵歸尚書省，宰相分判六尚書事。

translations.literal: Zao, because Jiang and Wu long resented fiscal commissioners who monopolized profit and deceived the throne, memorialized that circuit commissioners and prefects choose officials to deliver the two taxes to the capital, abolished circuit water-land transport commissioners, fiscal inspection offices, and the Jianghuai transport commissioner, returned fiscal and salt-iron affairs to the Department of State Affairs, and had chancellors divide the six ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao, reflecting Jiangnan resentment of profit-grubbing fiscal commissioners, had circuit commissioners and prefects send the two taxes directly, abolished transport commissioners and fiscal inspection offices, restored fiscal and salt-iron affairs to the Department of State Affairs, and split the six ministries among the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 以戶部侍郎元琇判諸道鹽鐵、榷酒，侍郎吉中孚判度支諸道兩稅。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Yuan Xiu was assigned all-circuit salt-iron and liquor monopoly; Vice Minister Ji Zhongfu was assigned fiscal two-tax affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu took salt-iron and liquor monopoly; Ji Zhongfu took fiscal two-tax affairs.

sentences.zh: 增江淮之運，浙江東、西歲運米七十五萬石，復以兩稅易米百萬石，江西、湖南、鄂岳、福建、嶺南米亦百二十萬石，詔浙江東、西節度使韓滉，淮南節度使杜亞運至東、西渭橋倉。

translations.literal: Jianghuai transport was increased: east and west Zhejiang 750,000 shi yearly, another million shi exchanged from the two taxes, and Jiangxi, Hunan, Eyue, Fujian, and Lingnan another 1.2 million shi; Han Huang of Zhejiang east-west and Du Ya of Huainan were ordered to deliver to the east and west Wei Bridge granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Jianghuai quotas: 750,000 shi from both Zhejiangs, a million from tax swaps, 1.2 million from Jiangxi, Hunan, Eyue, Fujian, and Lingnan, ordering Han Huang and Du Ya to deliver to the Wei Bridge granaries.

sentences.zh: 諸道有鹽鐵處，復置巡院。

translations.literal: Where circuits had salt and iron, inspection offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Salt-iron circuits regained inspection offices.

sentences.zh: 歲終宰相計課最。

translations.literal: At year's end chancellors reckoned performance rankings.
translations.idiomatic: At year-end the chancellors graded officials' performance.

sentences.zh: 崔造厚元琇，而韓滉方領轉運，奏國漕不可改。

translations.literal: Cui Zao favored Yuan Xiu, but Han Huang was then heading transport and memorialized that national canal transport could not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao favored Yuan Xiu, but Han Huang, still running transport, insisted the canal system could not be dismantled.

sentences.zh: 帝亦雅器滉，復以為江淮轉運使。

translations.literal: The emperor also esteemed Huang and again made him Jianghuai transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued Huang and restored him as Jianghuai transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元琇嫉其剛，不可共事，因有隙。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiu resented his harshness and could not work with him, and so a rift arose.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu despised his harshness; they could not cooperate and a feud opened.

sentences.zh: 琇稱疾罷，而滉為度支、諸道鹽鐵、轉運使，於是崔造亦罷。

translations.literal: Xiu pleaded illness and left office; Huang became fiscal, all-circuit salt-iron, and transport commissioner, and then Cui Zao was also removed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu quit citing illness; Huang took fiscal, salt-iron, and transport power, and Cui Zao fell soon after.

sentences.zh: 滉遂劾琇常餫米淄青、河中，而李納、懷光倚以構叛，貶琇雷州司戶參軍，尋賜死。

translations.literal: Huang then impeached Xiu for regularly shipping grain to Ziqing and Hezhong, on which Li Na and Huai Guang relied to plot rebellion; Xiu was demoted to Leizhou registrar and soon ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: Huang accused Yuan Xiu of feeding Ziqing and Hezhong, fueling Li Na and Zhu Ci's rebellions; he was demoted to Leizhou and then ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 是時，汴宋節度使春夏遣官監汴水，察盜灌溉者。

translations.literal: At this time the Bian-Song military commissioner in spring and summer sent officials to supervise the Bian River and investigate those who stole water for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring and summer the Bian-Song commissioner posted officials to guard the Bian Canal against illegal irrigation.

sentences.zh: 歲漕經底柱，覆者幾半。

translations.literal: Annual canal transport passing Dizhu nearly half was lost in capsizing.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly half the annual fleet was lost at the Dizhu reefs.

sentences.zh: 河中有山號「米堆」，運舟入三門，雇平陸人為門匠，執標指麾，一舟百日乃能上。

translations.literal: In the river was a hill called "Rice Mound"; transport boats entering Sanmen hired Pinglu men as gate craftsmen to hold markers and direct—a single boat needed a hundred days to get through.
translations.idiomatic: A reef called Rice Mound stood in the gorge; barges entering Sanmen hired Pinglu pilots called gate craftsmen to pole them through—a single vessel could take a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：「古無門匠墓。

translations.literal: A proverb says: "In antiquity there were no gate craftsmen's tombs."
translations.idiomatic: A proverb ran: "Of old there were no gate craftsmen's graves."

sentences.zh: 」謂皆溺死也。

translations.literal: " meaning they all drowned.
translations.idiomatic: —meaning they all drowned.

sentences.zh: 陝虢觀察使李泌益鑿集津倉山西逕為運道，屬于三門倉，治上路以回空車，費錢五萬緡，下路減半；

translations.literal: Shan-Guo observation commissioner Li Bi further cut a transport path west of Jijin Granary linking to Sanmen Granary, built the upper road for returning empty carts at fifty thousand strings, the lower road half that;
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi of Shan-Guo cut a western bypass from Jijin Granary to Sanmen, built an upper haul road for empty carts costing fifty thousand strings and a lower road half as much;

sentences.zh: 又為入渭船，方五板，輸東渭橋太倉米至凡百三十萬石，遂罷南路陸運。

translations.literal: he also made Wei-entry boats of five planks, delivering Ever-Normal Granary grain at East Wei Bridge up to 1.3 million shi in all, and then abolished the southern overland route.
translations.idiomatic: built five-plank Wei barges that moved 1.3 million shi from the Ever-Normal Granary at East Wei Bridge, and ended the southern overland route.

sentences.zh: 其後諸道鹽鐵、轉運使張滂復置江淮巡院。

translations.literal: Later all-circuit salt-iron and transport commissioner Zhang Pang restored the Jianghuai inspection office.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Pang restored the Jianghuai inspection office.

sentences.zh: 及浙西觀察使李錡領使，江淮堰埭隸浙西者，增私路小堰之稅，以副使潘孟陽主上都留後。

translations.literal: When Zhexi observation commissioner Li Qian headed the commission, on Jianghuai dams under Zhexi he added taxes on private-path small weirs, with Vice Commissioner Pan Mengyang managing the capital's rear office.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qian of Zhexi took the commission, he taxed private weirs on Zhexi-controlled Jianghuai dams while deputy Pan Mengyang ran the capital rear office.

sentences.zh: 李巽為諸道轉運、鹽鐵使，以堰埭歸鹽鐵使，罷其增置者。

translations.literal: Li Xun as all-circuit transport and salt-iron commissioner returned dams and weirs to the salt-iron office and abolished the added levies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun returned the dams to the salt-iron office and abolished the extra taxes.

sentences.zh: 自劉晏後，江淮米至渭橋寖減矣，至巽乃復如晏之多。

translations.literal: After Liu Yan, Jianghuai grain reaching Wei Bridge had gradually declined; only with Xun did it again match Yan's volume.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yan, Jianghuai grain to Wei Bridge had dwindled; only under Li Xun did volumes match Liu Yan's again.

sentences.zh: 初，揚州疏太子港、陳登塘，凡三十四陂，以益漕河，輒復堙塞。

translations.literal: At first Yangzhou dredged Taizi Harbor and Chendeng Pond, thirty-four embankments in all, to augment the canal river, but they were repeatedly silted shut again.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou had dredged Taizi Harbor, Chendeng Pond, and thirty-four reservoirs to feed the canal, but they kept silting shut again.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使杜亞乃濬渠蜀岡，疏句城湖、愛敬陂，起隄貫城，以通大舟。

translations.literal: Huainan military commissioner Du Ya then dredged the Shugang channel, opened Jucheng Lake and Aijing Embankment, and raised dikes through the city to admit large boats.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya of Huainan dredged the Shugang canal, opened Jucheng Lake and Aijing Embankment, and built city dikes so large vessels could pass.

sentences.zh: 河益庳，水下走淮，夏則舟不得前。

translations.literal: The river grew shallower, water ran down toward the Huai, and in summer boats could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The channel grew shallower, water drained toward the Huai, and summer left boats stranded.

sentences.zh: 節度使李吉甫築平津堰，以洩有餘，防不足，漕流遂通。

translations.literal: Military commissioner Li Jifu built the Pingjin Weir to release surplus and guard against shortage, and canal flow was then open.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu built the Pingjin Weir to spill excess water and hold back shortages, and the canal ran clear again.

sentences.zh: 然漕益少，江淮米至渭橋者纔二十萬斛。

translations.literal: Yet canal transport grew even less; Jianghuai grain reaching Wei Bridge was only two hundred thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: Yet transport kept shrinking, and only two hundred thousand hu of Jianghuai grain reached Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 諸道鹽鐵、轉運使盧坦糴以備一歲之費，省冗職八十員。

translations.literal: All-circuit salt-iron and transport commissioner Lu Tan bought grain to cover a year's expenses and cut eighty redundant posts.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tan bought grain for a year's supply and cut eighty redundant posts.

sentences.zh: 自江以南，補署皆剸屬院監，而漕米亡耗於路頗多。

translations.literal: South of the river, all appointments were wholly subordinate to inspection-office supervisors, and much canal grain was lost on the road.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze every post answered to inspection-office supervisors, and grain losses in transit were heavy.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎王播代坦，建議米至渭橋五百石亡五十石者死。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Vice Minister Wang Bo replaced Tan and proposed that if five hundred shi reached Wei Bridge with fifty shi lost, death was the penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo of the Ministry of Justice replaced him and proposed death for losing fifty shi out of every five hundred delivered to Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 其後判度支皇甫鎛議萬斛亡三百斛者償之，千七百斛者流塞下，過者死；

translations.literal: Later fiscal vice commissioner Huangfu Bo proposed that for ten thousand hu, loss of three hundred hu required compensation; 1,700 hu meant exile beyond the passes, and beyond that death;
translations.idiomatic: Later Huangfu Bo of the fiscal office required compensation for three hundred hu lost per ten thousand, exile beyond the passes for 1,700 hu lost, and death beyond that;

sentences.zh: 盜十斛者流，三十斛者死。

translations.literal: theft of ten hu meant exile, thirty hu meant death.
translations.idiomatic: theft of ten hu meant exile and thirty hu meant death.

sentences.zh: 而覆船敗輓，至者不得十之四五。

translations.literal: Yet with capsized boats and failed hauls, arrivals did not reach four or five tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Yet capsizes and wrecked hauls meant less than half the cargo arrived.

sentences.zh: 部吏舟人相挾為姦，榜笞號苦之聲聞于道路，禁錮連歲，赦下而獄死者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Department clerks and boatmen colluded in fraud; the sound of flogging and cries of pain were heard on the roads; imprisonment ran year after year, and after amnesties those dead in prison could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and boatmen colluded in fraud; flogging and cries of pain echoed along the roads; prisoners languished for years, and even after amnesties the dead in custody were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 其後貸死刑，流天德五城，人不畏法，運米至者十亡七八。

translations.literal: Later capital punishment was commuted to exile to the Tiande Five Cities; people did not fear the law, and of grain transported, seven or eight tenths were lost.
translations.idiomatic: When death sentences were commuted to exile in the Tiande Five Cities, the law lost its terror and seven or eight tenths of grain never arrived.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵、轉運使柳公綽請如王播議加重刑。

translations.literal: Salt-iron and transport commissioner Liu Gongchuo requested penalties as heavy as Wang Bo's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongchuo asked to restore Wang Bo's harsh penalties.

sentences.zh: 大和初，歲旱河涸，掊沙而進，米多耗，抵死甚眾，不待覆奏。

translations.literal: Early in Dahe, drought dried the river; they dug through sand to advance, grain was much wasted, and very many were put to death without awaiting review.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dahe a drought bared the riverbed; crews dug through sand, grain spoiled, and many were executed without awaiting imperial review.

sentences.zh: 奏、漢時故漕興成堰，東達永豐倉，咸陽縣令韓遼請疏之，自咸陽抵潼關三百里，可以罷車輓之勞。

translations.literal: The Qin-Han-era canal Xingcheng Weir, reaching east to Yongfeng Granary—Xianyang Magistrate Han Liao requested dredging it; from Xianyang to Tong Pass three hundred li could end cart-haul labor.
translations.idiomatic: Han Liao, magistrate of Xianyang, asked to dredge the Qin-Han Xingcheng Weir reaching Yongfeng Granary—a three-hundred-li waterway from Xianyang to Tong Pass that could end cart haulage.

sentences.zh: 宰相李固言以為非時，文宗曰：「苟利於人，陰陽拘忌，非朕所顧也。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Guyan held it untimely; Wenzong said: "If it benefits the people, yin-yang taboos are not what I heed.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Guyan called the timing wrong; Wenzong said, "If it helps the people, I will not be bound by yin-yang taboos.

sentences.zh: 」議遂決。

translations.literal: " The plan was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: " The project went ahead.

sentences.zh: 堰成，罷輓車之牛以供農耕，關中賴其利。

translations.literal: When the weir was finished, haul-cart oxen were released for farming, and Guanzhong relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: When the weir was finished, haul oxen returned to the fields and Guanzhong prospered.

sentences.zh: 故事，州縣官充綱，送輕貨四萬，書上考。

translations.literal: By precedent, prefecture and county officials served as convoy leaders; delivering forty thousand in light goods earned a top evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, county officials led convoys; delivering forty thousand in light goods earned top marks.

sentences.zh: 開成初，為長定綱，州擇清彊官送兩稅，至十萬遷一官，往來十年者授縣令。

translations.literal: Early in Kaicheng came the long-fixed convoy system: prefectures chose capable officials to deliver the two taxes; at one hundred thousand promotion came one rank, and after ten years of round trips one received county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Early Kaicheng introduced long-fixed convoys: prefectures chose capable men to deliver the two taxes; one hundred thousand earned a promotion, ten years of service earned a county magistracy.

sentences.zh: 江淮錢積河陰，轉輸歲費十七萬餘緡，行綱多以盜抵死。

translations.literal: Jianghuai coin piled up at Heyin; relay transport cost over 170,000 strings yearly, and many convoy leaders died for theft.
translations.idiomatic: Jianghuai coin piled up at Heyin; relay costs exceeded 170,000 strings a year, and many convoy leaders were executed for theft.

sentences.zh: 判度支王彥威置縣遞羣畜萬三千三百乘，使路傍民養以取傭，日役一驛，省費甚博。

translations.literal: Fiscal vice commissioner Wang Yanwei set up county relays with 13,300 draft animals in herds, had roadside people raise them for hire, one post station per day, saving costs greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanwei of the fiscal office fielded 13,300 relay animals raised by roadside households for hire, one post a day, at great savings.

sentences.zh: 而宰相亦以長定綱命官不以材，江淮大州，歲授官者十餘人，乃罷長定綱，送五萬者書上考，七萬者減一選，五十萬減三選而已。

translations.literal: Yet chancellors also appointed long-fixed convoy officials without regard to talent; in great Jianghuai prefectures more than ten officials were assigned yearly, so the long-fixed convoy was abolished—five thousand earned top marks, seventy thousand cut one selection, five hundred thousand cut three selections only.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors also appointed convoy leaders without regard to talent; large Jianghuai prefectures posted more than ten men a year, so the long-fixed convoy was scrapped—fifty thousand earned top marks, seventy thousand one fewer selection, five hundred thousand three fewer.

sentences.zh: 及戶部侍郎裴休為使，以河瀕縣令董漕事，自江達渭，運米四十萬石。

translations.literal: When Vice Minister Pei Xiu became commissioner, river-bank county magistrates oversaw canal affairs; from the river to the Wei, four hundred thousand shi of rice were transported.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Xiu became commissioner, river-bank magistrates ran canal affairs and moved four hundred thousand shi from the Yangtze to the Wei.

sentences.zh: 居三歲，米至渭橋百二十萬石。

translations.literal: After three years, grain reaching Wei Bridge was 1.2 million shi.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years deliveries to Wei Bridge reached 1.2 million shi.

sentences.zh: 凡漕達于京師而足國用者，大略如此。

translations.literal: Canal transport reaching the capital to supply state needs was broadly like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the broad outline of canal transport that fed the capital and the state.

sentences.zh: 其他州、縣、方鎮，漕以自資，或兵所征行，轉運以給一時之用者，皆不足紀。

translations.literal: Other prefectures, counties, and military commissions using canal transport for their own funds, or armies on campaign with relay supply for temporary needs, are not worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Local canal hauls for prefectures, counties, and garrisons, or wartime relays, are not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 唐開軍府以扞要衝，因隙地置營田，天下屯總九百九十二。

translations.literal: The Tang opened military prefectures to guard strategic points and on vacant land established garrison farms; garrisons nationwide totaled 992.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang opened military prefectures on key frontiers and established garrison farms on spare land; nationwide there were 992 garrisons.

sentences.zh: 司農寺每屯三十頃，州、鎮諸軍每屯五十頃。

translations.literal: The Court of the Imperial Granaries allotted thirty qing per garrison; prefectural and garrison armies fifty qing per garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Granary garrisons farmed thirty qing each; prefectural and frontier armies fifty qing each.

sentences.zh: 水陸腴瘠、播殖地宜與其功庸煩省、收率之多少，皆決於尚書省。

translations.literal: Fertility by water and land, suitability for planting, labor required, and yield rates were all decided by the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soil quality, crop suitability, labor costs, and expected yields were all set by the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 苑內屯以善農者為屯官、屯副，御史巡行莅輸。

translations.literal: Park garrisons appointed skilled farmers as garrison chief and deputy; censors toured to oversee delivery.
translations.idiomatic: Park garrisons named skilled farmers as chiefs and deputies, with censors touring to inspect deliveries.

sentences.zh: 上地五十畝，瘠地二十畝，稻田八十畝，則給牛一。

translations.literal: Fifty mu of good land, twenty mu of poor land, or eighty mu of paddy—then one ox was supplied.
translations.idiomatic: One ox was allotted per fifty mu of good land, twenty mu of poor land, or eighty mu of paddy.

sentences.zh: 諸屯以地良薄與歲之豐凶為三等，具民田歲穫多少，取中熟為率。

translations.literal: All garrisons graded land quality and yearly harvest into three ranks, tallying civilian field yields and taking mid-harvest as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons graded plots and harvests in three tiers against civilian yields, using an average year as the benchmark.

sentences.zh: 有警，則以兵若夫千人助收。

translations.literal: When there was alarm, a thousand soldiers or laborers aided the harvest.
translations.idiomatic: In emergencies a thousand troops or laborers were sent to help harvest.

sentences.zh: 隸司農者，歲三月，卿、少卿循行，治不法者。

translations.literal: Those under the Imperial Granaries: each third month the director and vice director toured and punished lawbreakers.
translations.idiomatic: Granary garrisons were inspected every third month by the director and vice director, who punished violations.

sentences.zh: 凡屯田收多者，褒進之。

translations.literal: Garrison farms with high yields were commended and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: High-yield garrisons were commended and promoted.

sentences.zh: 歲以仲春籍來歲頃畝、州府軍鎮之遠近，上兵部，度便宜遣之。

translations.literal: Each mid-spring they registered next year's acreage and distances of prefectures, armies, and garrisons, reported to the Ministry of War, and dispatched as expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Each mid-spring they registered next year's acreage and relay distances, reported to the Ministry of War, and deployed forces as needed.

sentences.zh: 開元二十五年，詔屯官敍功以歲豐凶為上下。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, an edict ranked garrison officers' merit by whether the year was bountiful or lean.
translations.idiomatic: In 737 an edict ranked garrison officers by harvest quality.

sentences.zh: 鎮戍地可耕者，人給十畝以供糧。

translations.literal: Where garrison land could be farmed, each man was given ten mu for rations.
translations.idiomatic: Where garrison land could be tilled, each man received ten mu for his rations.

sentences.zh: 方春，屯官巡行，讁作不時者。

translations.literal: In spring, garrison chiefs toured and rebuked those who farmed out of season.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring garrison chiefs toured and punished untimely planting.

sentences.zh: 天下屯田收穀百九十餘萬斛。

translations.literal: Nationwide garrison farms harvested more than 1.9 million hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Nationwide garrison farms harvested more than 1.9 million hu.

sentences.zh: 初，度支歲市糧於北都，以贍振武、天德、靈武、鹽、夏之軍，費錢五六十萬緡，泝河舟溺甚眾。

translations.literal: At first the fiscal office yearly bought grain at the Northern Capital to supply the armies of Zhenwu, Tiande, Lingwu, Yan, and Xia, costing five or six hundred thousand strings, and many boats were lost going upriver.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the fiscal office bought grain yearly at Taiyuan to feed the Zhenwu, Tiande, Lingwu, Yan, and Xia armies at five or six hundred thousand strings, with heavy losses on the river route.

sentences.zh: 建中初，宰相楊炎請置屯田於豐州，發關輔民鑿陵陽渠以增溉。

translations.literal: Early in Jianzhong, Chancellor Yang Yan requested garrison farms at Fengzhou and mobilized Guanfu people to cut the Lingyang Canal for more irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong, Chancellor Yang Yan proposed garrison farms at Fengzhou and conscripted Guanfu labor to cut the Lingyang Canal.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹嚴郢嘗從事朔方，知其利害，以為不便，疏奏不報。

translations.literal: Jingzhao Intendant Yan Ying had once served in Shuofang and knew the pros and cons; he held it inexpedient and memorialized, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying of Jingzhao, who had served in Shuofang, saw the drawbacks and memorialized against it without response.

sentences.zh: 郢又奏：「五城舊屯，其數至廣，以開渠之糧貸諸城，約以冬輸；

translations.literal: Ying memorialized again: "The old garrisons of the Five Cities are very numerous; lend canal-opening grain to the cities with delivery promised in winter;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying argued again: "The old Five Cities garrisons are vast—lend canal grain to the garrisons for winter delivery;

sentences.zh: 又以開渠功直布帛先給田者，據估轉穀。

translations.literal: also pay canal labor value in cloth and silk first to those given fields, converting by appraisal into grain.
translations.idiomatic: pay canal workers in cloth and silk upfront, then convert to grain at appraised rates.

sentences.zh: 如此則關輔免調發，五城田闢，比之浚渠利十倍也。

translations.literal: Thus Guanfu would be spared levies, Five Cities fields opened, and the profit would be tenfold compared with dredging the canal.
translations.idiomatic: Guanfu would avoid levies, the Five Cities fields would open, and the gain would be ten times dredging the canal."

sentences.zh: 」時楊炎方用事，郢議不用，而陵陽渠亦不成。

translations.literal: " Yang Yan was then in power; Yan Ying's plan was not used, and the Lingyang Canal was also not completed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan was in power, Yan Ying's plan was ignored, and the Lingyang Canal was never finished.

sentences.zh: 然振武、天德良田，廣袤千里。

translations.literal: Yet Zhenwu and Tiande had fine fields stretching a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhenwu and Tiande still had fine fields stretching a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 元和中，振武軍饑，宰相李絳請開營田，可省度支漕運及絕和糴欺隱。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era the Zhenwu army starved; Chancellor Li Jiang requested opening garrison farms to save fiscal canal transport and end fair-purchase fraud.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe, starving Zhenwu troops led Chancellor Li Jiang to propose garrison farms to cut fiscal transport costs and fair-purchase fraud.

sentences.zh: 憲宗稱善，乃以韓重華為振武、京西營田、和糴、水運使，起代北，墾田三百頃，出贓罪吏九百餘人，給以耒耜、耕牛，假種糧，使償所負粟，二歲大熟。

translations.literal: Xianzong approved and appointed Han Chonghua Zhenwu and Jingxi garrison-farm, fair-purchase, and water-transport commissioner; starting north of Dai, he opened three hundred qing, released over nine hundred corrupt officials, gave plows and oxen, lent seed grain, had them repay owed grain, and in two years there was great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong approved and made Han Chonghua commissioner; north of Dai he opened three hundred qing, paroled nine hundred corrupt officials with plows, oxen, and seed on condition they repay grain debts, and reaped a great harvest in two years.

sentences.zh: 因募人為十五屯，每屯百三十人，人耕百畝，就高為堡，東起振武，西逾雲州，極於中受降城，凡六百餘里，列柵二十，墾田三千八百餘頃，歲收粟二十萬石，省度支錢二千餘萬緡。

translations.literal: He then recruited men for fifteen garrisons, 130 men each, each farming a hundred mu, building forts on high ground from Zhenwu east to beyond Yunzhou to Central Accept-Submission City—over six hundred li, twenty palisades, more than 3,800 qing opened, 200,000 shi yearly, saving over twenty million strings for the fiscal office.
translations.idiomatic: He raised fifteen garrisons of 130 men each farming a hundred mu, building hill forts from Zhenwu to Central Accept-Submission City—six hundred li, twenty palisades, 3,800 qing opened, 200,000 shi a year, saving over twenty million strings.

sentences.zh: 重華入朝，奏請益開田五千頃，法用人七千，可以盡給五城。

translations.literal: Chonghua came to court and requested opening another five thousand qing, using seven thousand men by regulation, which could fully supply the Five Cities.
translations.idiomatic: At court he asked to open another five thousand qing with seven thousand men to fully supply the Five Cities.

sentences.zh: 會李絳已罷，後宰相持其議而止。

translations.literal: Li Jiang had already left office; later chancellors held to their objections and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang had fallen; later chancellors blocked the plan.

sentences.zh: 憲宗末，天下營田皆雇民或借庸以耕，又以瘠地易上地，民間苦之。

translations.literal: Late in Xianzong, nationwide garrison farms all hired civilians or borrowed corvée to farm, and exchanged poor land for good land—the people suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xianzong, garrison farms hired civilians or corvée labor and swapped poor plots for good ones at the people's expense.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，詔還所易地，而耕以官兵。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, an edict returned the exchanged land and farming was done by officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong ordered the exchanged land returned and put farming back in soldiers' hands.

sentences.zh: 耕官地者，給三之一以終身。

translations.literal: Those farming government land received one-third for life.
translations.idiomatic: Those who farmed government land kept one-third of the yield for life.

sentences.zh: 靈武、邠寧，土廣肥而民不知耕。

translations.literal: Lingwu and Binning had broad fertile soil yet the people did not know how to farm.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwu and Binning had broad fertile soil, yet the people scarcely farmed it.

sentences.zh: 大和末，王起奏立營田。

translations.literal: Late in Dahe, Wang Qi memorialized to establish garrison farms.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Dahe, Wang Qi proposed establishing garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 後党項大擾河西，邠寧節度使畢諴亦募士開營田，歲收三十萬斛，省度支錢數百萬緡。

translations.literal: Later the Tangut greatly disturbed Hexi; Binning military commissioner Bi Dan also recruited men to open garrison farms, harvesting 300,000 hu yearly and saving several million strings for the fiscal office.
translations.idiomatic: When Tangut raids shook Hexi, Bi Dan of Binning recruited colonists, harvested 300,000 hu a year, and saved millions of strings.

sentences.zh: 貞觀、開元後，邊土西舉高昌、龜茲、焉耆、小勃律，北抵薛延陀故地，緣邊數十州戍重兵，營田及地租不足以供軍，於是初有和糴。

translations.literal: After Zhenguan and Kaiyuan, the frontier west took Gaochang, Kucha, Yanqi, and Little Bolü, north to the old Xueyantuo lands; dozens of border prefectures garrisoned heavy troops, and garrison farms plus land tax could not supply the armies—thus fair purchase began.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenguan and Kaiyuan the frontier stretched west to Gaochang and Kucha and north to the old Xueyantuo lands; dozens of border prefectures held heavy garrisons that garrison farms and land tax could not feed—so fair purchase began.

sentences.zh: 牛仙客為相，有彭果者獻策廣關輔之糴，京師糧稟益羨，自是玄宗不復幸東都。

translations.literal: When Niu Xianke was chancellor, a Peng Guo presented a plan to expand Guanfu fair purchase; the capital's grain stores grew abundant, and from then Xuanzong no longer visited the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chancellor Niu Xianke, Peng Guo proposed expanding Guanfu fair purchase; capital granaries overflowed, and Xuanzong never again visited Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，歲以錢六十萬緡賦諸道和糴，斗增三錢，每歲短遞輸京倉者百餘萬斛。

translations.literal: In Tianbao, yearly six hundred thousand strings were assessed on circuits for fair purchase, three cash added per dou, and each year over a million hu were relayed short-haul to the capital granary.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao, circuits paid six hundred thousand strings yearly for fair purchase with three cash per dou added; more than a million hu reached the capital granary each year.

sentences.zh: 米賤則少府加估而糴，貴則賤價而糶。

translations.literal: When rice was cheap the Imperial Treasury added to the price and bought; when dear, sold at low price.
translations.idiomatic: When rice was cheap the treasury bought at a premium; when dear, it sold at a discount.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，吐蕃劫盟，召諸道兵十七萬戍邊。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenyuan the Tibetans broke the treaty; troops from all circuits, 170,000, were summoned to garrison the border.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan, after the Tibetans broke the peace treaty, 170,000 troops from every circuit were posted to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 關中為吐蕃蹂躪者二十年矣，北至河曲，人戶無幾，諸道戍兵月給粟十七萬斛，皆糴於關中。

translations.literal: Guanzhong had been ravaged by Tibetans for twenty years; north to Hequ few households remained; border garrisons monthly received 170,000 hu of grain, all bought in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong had been ravaged by Tibetans for twenty years; north to Hequ almost no households remained; border garrisons needed 170,000 hu a month, all bought in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 宰相陸贄以「關中穀賤，請和糴，可至百餘萬斛。

translations.literal: Chancellor Lu Zhi held: "Grain in Guanzhong is cheap; request fair purchase, which can reach more than a million hu.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Lu Zhi argued: "Guanzhong grain is cheap—fair purchase could reach more than a million hu.

sentences.zh: 計諸縣船車至太倉，穀價四十有餘，米價七十，則一年和糴之數當轉運之二年，一斗轉運之資當和糴之五斗。

translations.literal: Calculating boats and carts from all counties to the Ever-Normal Granary—grain over forty, rice seventy—then one year's fair purchase equals two years of transport, and one dou's transport cost equals five dou of fair purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Boats and carts from the counties to the Ever-Normal Granary cost over forty for grain and seventy for rice—one year of fair purchase equals two years of transport, and one dou of transport cost equals five dou of fair purchase.

sentences.zh: 減轉運以實邊，存轉運以備時要。

translations.literal: Reduce transport to fill the border, keep transport for timely need.
translations.idiomatic: Cut transport to stock the frontier, keep enough for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 江淮米至河陰者罷八十萬斛，河陰米至太原倉者罷五十萬，太原米至東渭橋者罷二十萬。

translations.literal: Jianghuai grain to Heyin could be cut by 800,000 hu, Heyin to Taiyuan Granary by 500,000, Taiyuan to East Wei Bridge by 200,000.
translations.idiomatic: Cut Jianghuai-to-Heyin by 800,000 hu, Heyin-to-Taiyuan by 500,000, and Taiyuan-to-East Wei Bridge by 200,000.

sentences.zh: 以所減米糶江淮水菑州縣，斗減時五十以救乏。

translations.literal: Sell the saved grain in Jianghuai flood-stricken prefectures and counties, cutting fifty cash from the current price per dou to relieve distress.
translations.idiomatic: Sell the saved grain in flood-hit Jianghuai counties at fifty cash below market to relieve distress.

sentences.zh: 京城東渭橋之糴，斗增時三十以利農。

translations.literal: Fair purchase at the capital's East Wei Bridge would add thirty cash to the current price per dou to benefit farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Fair purchase at East Wei Bridge in the capital would add thirty cash per dou to help farmers.

sentences.zh: 以江淮糶米及減運直市絹帛送上都。

translations.literal: Use Jianghuai sold grain and saved transport costs to buy silk and cloth for the supreme capital.
translations.idiomatic: Use Jianghuai grain sales and transport savings to buy silk for the capital."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃命度支增估糴粟三十三萬斛，然不能盡用贄議。

translations.literal: " The emperor then ordered the fiscal office to buy 330,000 hu at added price, yet could not fully adopt Zhi's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the fiscal office to buy 330,000 hu at premium prices, but did not fully adopt Lu Zhi's plan.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位之初，有司以歲豐熟，請畿內和糴。

translations.literal: Early in Xianzong's accession, the departments, because the year was abundant, requested fair purchase within the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianzong's reign, officials requested capital-region fair purchase because the harvest was abundant.

sentences.zh: 當時府、縣配戶督限，有稽違則迫蹙鞭撻，甚於稅賦，號為和糴，其實害民。

translations.literal: Then prefectures and counties assigned quotas household by household; delay brought coercion and flogging worse than tax collection—it was called fair purchase, but in truth it harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties assigned household quotas; delays brought coercion and flogging worse than taxation—called fair purchase, it truly harmed the people.
